- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak (e.g., +0.3+ after -0.4+), model underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to capture sentiment shift.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–3 days ahead); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to initial forecast values.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day windows; if forecast shows strong upward trend beyond 10 days, reduce slope after day 10 to avoid overextension.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture latent bullish momentum.
